principle_text: When the persuadee responds with friendly but off-topic personal information, avoid focusing solely on casual rapport without steering the conversation toward the donation goal.
When the persuadee reveals personal involvement in charitable activities, you should acknowledge and build on this connection to encourage further engagement or support.
When the persuadee has shown prior charitable involvement, you should connect their past actions to your cause to make your donation request more relevant and personally meaningful.

When the persuadee responds positively but vaguely about their willingness to help, avoid relying solely on enthusiasm and broad questions that do not clearly advance commitment to the specific donation request.

When the persuadee expresses a willingness to help and a history of charitable giving, you should enthusiastically praise their generosity and clearly explain the tangible impact their donation will have.
When the persuadee shows willingness to give and values charity, you should use vivid, emotional examples of urgent needs to deepen engagement and prompt concrete donation discussions.
When the persuadee responds positively but without clear commitment, avoid rushing into the donation request without further rapport building or contextual engagement.
When the persuadee shows openness but limited commitment, you should make a clear, direct donation request with flexible options to encourage engagement and prompt further interest.

When the persuadee asks for more information about a charity's activities, avoid giving only a general description without clarifying the geographic scope or specific impact relevant to their concerns.

When the persuadee acknowledges the importance of the cause but asks neutral clarifying questions, avoid providing only factual information without addressing trust or organizational credibility concerns.
